title: Seeking in Space: Benchmarking Purposeful Active Exploration of Vision-Language Models for Spatial Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2611.31215v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Humans explore unfamiliar spaces with purpose, deciding where to look until they have gathered the evidence a spatial question requires. However, can vision-language models (VLMs), which reason increasingly well over curated images and videos, also seek in space when the evidence is not handed to them? We present ActSpace-Bench, a benchmark of 994 questions across 234 exploration episodes in 72 real-scanned indoor scenes, where a model starts from a single view, navigates real captured frames, and must gather evidence before answering. To assess whether such exploration is purposeful, we introduce a controlled evaluation protocol that fixes each model as the reasoner and compares its own exploration against a same-budget random walk and an oracle route, separating evidence seeking from spatial reasoning. Every question is verified to require exploration and answered from 3D annotations, masked-evidence questions test whether models know

translated_title: 在空间中寻找：基准测试视觉语言模型在空间推理中进行有目的的主动探索
translated_abstract: 人类在探索不熟悉的空间时是有目的的，会自主决定去哪里观察，直到收集到回答某个空间问题所需的证据。然而，在精心筛选的图像和视频上推理能力日益增强的视觉语言模型（VLM），当证据没有被直接提供给它们时，是否也能在空间中进行主动寻找？我们提出了ActSpace-Bench，这是一个包含994个问题、234个探索回合、覆盖72个真实扫描室内场景的基准测试。在该基准中，模型从单一视角出发，需要在真实采集的帧中进行导航，并且必须在回答之前主动收集证据。为了评估这种探索是否具有目的性，我们引入了一种受控评估协议：将每个模型固定为推理者，并将其自身的探索行为与同等预算下的随机游走路线和预言机（oracle）最优路线进行对比，从而将证据寻找能力与空间推理能力分离开来。每个问题均经过验证确认必须通过探索才能回答，并基于3D标注给出标准答案；此外，掩码证据问题用于测试模型是否知道（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了ActSpace-Bench基准，通过将模型自身探索与同等预算随机游走及预言机最优路线对比的受控评估协议，系统评估视觉语言模型在真实室内场景中进行有目的主动空间探索、并将证据寻找与空间推理分离的能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces ActSpace-Bench, a benchmark that systematically evaluates the purposeful active spatial exploration ability of vision-language models in real scanned indoor scenes, using a controlled protocol that compares each model's own exploration against a same-budget random walk and an oracle route to disentangle evidence seeking from spatial reasoning.
